title: Guide - Finding Rest - Letting go of the day

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Finding Rest. <short pause> This practice is called Letting Go of the Day. <short pause> There is nothing you need to finish here. <short pause> For the next few minutes, you only need to set some things down.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let yourself settle, sitting or lying down. <short pause> Feel what is holding you up... the bed, the chair, the floor beneath it all. <short pause> You don't have to hold yourself quite so tightly. <short pause> Take an easy breath in... <short pause> and let it go.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: The body often stops before the day does. <short pause> You switch off the light, and there it is again... the message you didn't answer, the thing you said at lunch, the job that is only half done. <short pause> It's as if the day followed you down the hall, still talking.

Long ago, someone who had been through great trouble learned to speak kindly to their own soul. <short pause> They had cried out to God, and they had been heard. <short pause> These are their words, from Psalm one hundred sixteen, verse seven.
Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the Lord hath dealt bountifully with thee. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Return unto thy rest. <short pause> Return... as if rest is a home you already have. <short pause> You don't have to build it tonight. <short pause> You only have to turn back toward it.

And notice the reason. <short pause> It isn't that everything got done. <short pause> It is that the Lord has been good. <short pause> Your rest can lean on His goodness, even when your list is unfinished.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So let's walk gently back through your day, and leave it with Him. <short pause> Begin with the morning. <short pause> See the first room you stood in, and the first thing that needed you. <short pause> Don't judge it. Just notice it... <short pause> and as you breathe out, say quietly within, Lord, the morning is Yours.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Now the middle of the day. <short pause> The faces you saw. The work in your hands. <short pause> Perhaps a moment that went well, and a moment you would like to have back. <short pause> Let both of them be there. <short pause> Breathe in softly... <short pause> and as you breathe out, Lord, the afternoon is Yours.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And now this evening. <short pause> Whatever was said, and whatever was left unsaid. <short pause> The dishes, the door, the last thing you looked at before you came here. <short pause> Breathe in once more... <short pause> and as you breathe out, Lord, the evening is Yours.

Is there one thing that still doesn't want to be put down? <short pause> You can give it a name. <short pause> Then picture yourself laying it on a table beside you. <short pause> It will be safe there. <short pause> If it needs you tomorrow, you can pick it up with rested hands.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now let the body follow. <short pause> Let your forehead smooth. <short pause> Let your jaw loosen. <short pause> Let your shoulders drop away from your ears. <short pause> Let your hands open... just a little. <short pause> Open hands have finished carrying.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, <short pause> thank You for every kindness in this day, the ones I saw and the ones I missed. <short pause> Forgive what I did poorly. <short pause> Keep what I could not finish. <short pause> I place this whole day in Your care, and I return to my rest in You. <short pause> Amen.

If the day starts talking again, you don't need to argue with it. <short pause> Just breathe out, and answer softly... <short pause> return unto thy rest, O my soul. <short pause> The day is in good hands now. <short pause> Rest well.
